content:
Meta Ads Research: Web Page Data (for Bobby)

Purpose: Structured content for Bobby to build a webpage on aheadofmarket.com showcasing AOM's HVAC advertising research. This page serves as a sales tool for Jacob's outreach and proof of AOM's market expertise.

Page Structure

Hero Section

Title: Your Competitors Are Already Advertising. Are You? Subtitle: We analyzed every active Facebook and Instagram ad from Arizona's top HVAC companies. Here's what we found. CTA Button: "Get Your Free Ad Strategy Session"

Section 1: The Big Number

Stat Block:

  • 7 out of 10 major Arizona HVAC companies are running paid Meta ads right now
  • $0.69 average cost per click on Facebook (vs $29+ on Google)
  • $18-$45 cost per lead during peak season
  • 32% lower cost per lead with video ads vs static images

Supporting Text: While most contractors rely on word-of-mouth and yard signs, the companies winning new business in 2026 are showing up in every homeowner's Facebook and Instagram feed. The data doesn't lie: paid social media advertising is the most cost-effective way to reach property owners in Arizona.

Section 2: Who's Running Ads (Company Profiles)

Section Title: Real Companies. Real Ads. Real Results. Section Subtitle: We pulled live data from Meta's Ad Library on March 10, 2026. Here's who's spending money to win your customers.

Card Layout (grid of company cards):

Card 1: George Brazil

  • 4 active campaigns
  • All launched March 2, 2026
  • Offers: $59 check-up, $1,500 off mini-split, $4,000 off HVAC system, furnace giveaway contest
  • Formats: Video + image carousel
  • Takeaway: "Multiple campaigns testing different price points simultaneously"

Card 2: Chas Roberts

  • 2 active campaigns
  • Running since January 2026
  • Offers: Free second opinion, lifetime warranty water heater
  • Format: Image ads with bold text overlay
  • Takeaway: "Targeting people who already got a competitor's quote"

Card 3: American Home Water & Air

  • 4 active campaigns (3 variants of same ad)
  • Revenue: $39M+
  • Offer: Save up to $3,100+ on high-efficiency AC
  • Format: Multiple ad variants for A/B testing
  • Takeaway: "Previous Facebook campaign delivered 31% revenue growth in 8 months"

Card 4: Brewer's AC

  • 5 active campaigns
  • Family-owned since 1982
  • Mix: Brand awareness + TRANE product partnerships
  • Takeaway: "Most diverse ad strategy of any company in this research"

Card 5: Ideal Air Conditioning

  • 6 active campaigns
  • Running continuously since September 2024 (18+ months)
  • Focus: HVAC + insulation, rebate stacking
  • Takeaway: "Companies don't run ads for 18 months if they aren't working"

Card 6: Ambient Edge

  • 4 active campaigns
  • Using ads for M&A announcements + education
  • Serves western AZ + Las Vegas
  • Takeaway: "Educational content positions them as the expert, not just a vendor"

Card 7: Francisco's Cooling & Heating

  • 1 active campaign
  • Hyper-local (Gilbert only)
  • Fear-based messaging about Arizona heat
  • Takeaway: "Even small companies can compete with targeted local ads"

Section 3: What's Working

Section Title: The Playbook Every Winning HVAC Ad Follows

Pattern 1: Specific Dollar Amounts

  • Never "great deals" or "affordable prices"
  • Always "$59 check-up" or "$3,100 savings" or "$4,000 off"
  • Real numbers build trust and set expectations

Pattern 2: Video First

  • 32% lower cost per lead vs static images
  • Vertical format (9:16) for mobile
  • Real footage from job sites, not stock video

Pattern 3: Local Identity

  • "Your neighbors" / "Locally owned since 1982"
  • City-specific targeting (Gilbert, Phoenix, Tempe)
  • Community engagement (furnace giveaway contests)

Pattern 4: Urgency + Fear

  • "Arizona heat can destroy your AC"
  • "Not happy with your HVAC quote?"
  • Seasonal timing (all campaigns launched Feb-Mar before summer)

Pattern 5: Multi-Campaign Testing

  • Top companies run 3-6 ads simultaneously
  • Different offers, formats, and audiences
  • Data-driven: keep what works, kill what doesn't

Section 4: The Gap

Section Title: Here's What Most Contractors Are Missing

Key Point: The biggest players (Parker & Sons at $210M revenue, Howard Air, Goettl) are NOT running Meta ads. They rely on Google, TV, and radio. Meanwhile, smaller companies like Francisco's ($500/month budget) are getting leads at $0.69 per click.

Stats to highlight:

  • 274+ HVAC contractors in Phoenix
  • Only ~30% have active Facebook pages
  • Less than 10% run paid Meta ads
  • Average HVAC company spends $9,000-$10,000/month on Google PPC
  • Facebook delivers the same leads for 1/40th the cost per click

Conclusion Line: "The companies investing in social media advertising today are building the brand recognition that wins tomorrow's contracts. The ones that wait will pay 10x more to catch up."

Section 5: CTA Section

Title: Ready to Show Up Where Your Customers Are Looking? Subtitle: AOM builds and manages complete social media advertising programs for contractors. Real content. Real strategy. Real results.

Bullet Points:

  • Custom video content from real job sites (not stock footage)
  • Facebook + Instagram ad campaigns built for your market
  • Monthly content calendar with consistent posting
  • Performance tracking and optimization
  • Starting at $3,000/month

CTA Button: "Book a Free Strategy Call" Secondary CTA: "See Our Work" (links to case studies / Ambition project)

Section 6: Additional Research Available

Title: We Do This Research for Every Client

Text: This HVAC research is just one example. AOM runs competitive ad analysis for every industry we serve. When you work with us, you get:

  • Complete competitive ad library analysis for your market
  • Audience targeting recommendations based on real data
  • Content strategy built on what's actually working (not guesswork)
  • Monthly reporting showing your ads vs. competitors

Design Notes for Bobby

  • Dark background, light text (matches AOM brand)
  • Company cards should be interactive (hover to expand details)
  • Stats should be large, bold numbers with supporting text below
  • Screenshots from Meta Ad Library can be used as proof (saved in /tmp/ on Patrik's machine)
  • Mobile-first: this page will be shared in cold emails, people will open on phones
  • "Old people can read em, young people love em" standard applies
  • Minimum 16px body text, high contrast throughout
  • CTA buttons should be prominent, repeated at least 3 times on the page

SEO Notes

  • Target keywords: "HVAC advertising Arizona," "HVAC Facebook ads Phoenix," "contractor social media marketing Arizona"
  • Meta description: "See which Arizona HVAC companies are running Facebook and Instagram ads in 2026. Real data from Meta's Ad Library, with actionable insights for contractors."
  • URL suggestion: aheadofmarket.com/research/hvac-ads-arizona
